items.claim: Uploading a file whose extension passes a naive extension check but whose content is executable (or is given executable handling) yields remote code execution through the web server.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as: When an attacker can upload arbitrary files to the back-end server, they can upload malicious files, like web shells, which would enable them to execute arbitrary commands on the back-end server. This eventually allows attackers to take control over the entire server and all web applications hosted on it, which makes `File Upload Attacks` among the most critical web vulnerabilities.

Write-up provenance: Esther7171/HackTheBox-Writeups-Walkthroughs :: Write-ups/Academy/05. Web Exploitation/31c. File Upload Attacks/File Upload Attacks.md (816 words, classified web).
items.disproof: Refuted when the upload is stored outside any served or executable path, or the content is rewritten to an inert type, so no interpreter ever executes the uploaded bytes.
